lines.en: 「Hospital room, 9:12 AM.」
―Everyone, meet at the industrial complex's east entrance by seven tomorrow evening. We're going beyond the [Final Wall] to rescue Kim Dokja.
Jung Heewon had received the message last night. The sender was Han Sooyoung. As always, it was an insolent message.
After receiving it, Jung Heewon had stood staring blankly out the window for a long time.
「Jung Heewon did not want to return to the scenarios.」
She had fought harder than any incarnation. More than anyone, she had wanted to save Kim Dokja and end the scenarios. And at last, she had made it here.
「The Final Wall she had seen in the scenarios' final chapter.」
Even now, she could remember it vividly whenever she closed her eyes.
The memory of fighting alongside Kim Dokja, who had become the ‘Enemy of the Story.’
Amid that dreadful flood of Stories, she had survived by cutting and cutting and cutting again. She had broken the wall and arrived at her final station.
「And yet Han Sooyoung was telling her to board that train once more.」
She was telling her to return to the place where the [Final Wall] had stood.
Saying they had left something on the train they had stepped off.
“Heewon-ssi.”
Only then did Jung Heewon realize that the hand gripping the curtain was trembling.
“Did you get it too, Hyunsung-ssi?”
“Yes.”
“What do you think?”
“······The Dokja-ssi we remember is here.”
The Kim Dokja they remembered was sleeping soundly. Eyelids that had forgotten every tragedy in the world. Jung Heewon gently covered his eyes with her hand.
Some misfortunes disappear if you simply don't look at them.
「This Kim Dokja was the Kim Dokja they remembered.」

Before their eyes was the Kim Dokja who had overcome Geumho Station, Chungmuro, Gwanghwamun, the Demon Realm, Olympus, Journey to the West, and the Final Wall alongside them. He remembered the ring of Jung Heewon's sword. He remembered Lee Hyunsung's trauma. He remembered his promises to his companions.
Exactly this much was the Kim Dokja they loved.
The Kim Dokja she wanted to protect.
She wondered whether it was right to divide a person so simply, but this wasn't merely a question of ‘Avatar.’
After all, when you liked someone, you liked a part of that person.
The bloodstains on Kim Dokja's wounds dissolved into smoke with a soft rustle.

Crumbling Stories drifted in the air, then scattered into the sky outside. Jung Heewon didn't know where they were going. Perhaps they were vanishing forever. Or perhaps they were returning to another Kim Dokja.
「The Kim Dokja who remembered ‘Ways of Survival’ and had always loved a single story.」
Jung Heewon did not know that Kim Dokja.
No one could love what they didn't know well.
“Hyunsung-ssi.”
“Yes.”
“If Dokja-ssi were in our place, what would he have done?”
Lee Hyunsung did not answer for a long time.
「Hospital room, 1:31 PM.」
Many people seemed to have visited already. Flowers and gifts lay neatly arranged on the hospital room's table. Gifts for when Kim Dokja might one day awaken.
After fiddling with a petal for a moment, Jang Hayoung slowly approached Kim Dokja.
“You're the Kim Dokja I remember. Right? The Kim Dokja who saved me in the Demon Realm.”
The clock beside his pillow was ticking.
The person who had made time flow again in the frozen 73rd Demon Realm.
The person who had spurred her to act when she had despaired before the wall of talent.
Demon King of Salvation.
“Actually, I didn't want to come back to Earth then.”
Jang Hayoung spoke with a bitter smile.
“I don't have a single good memory here.”
She was a dimensional mover.

As with most dimensional movers, the circumstances were inexplicable. One day, working late at her office as usual, she had suddenly felt a pain in her heart and collapsed. As her breathing stopped, she thought, ‘I worked too hard.’ If there was another life, she vowed, ‘I'll never work hard again.’ Then she opened her eyes in the Demon Realm.
Watching the industrial complex's residents hurry off to lunch, Jang Hayoung murmured.
“Thanks to you, I went and worked hard again.”
「Hospital room, 6:24 PM.」
“Flip it. Your turn.”
At Lee Gilyoung's words, Shin Yoosung tossed a hundred-won coin. It spun through the air and landed with a tap on the back of her hand. Heads.
“How many flips?”
“Ninety-nine.”
“Then it's forty-nine to fifty.”
As Lee Gilyoung dusted off his hands and stood, Lee Jihye asked from the caregiver's bed.
“Are you two making that bet again? The one about Dokja-ajusshi being alive if it comes up heads?”
“What are you talking about? Ajusshi's alive right here.”
“Then what are you betting on?”
The children said nothing. Lee Jihye frowned.
“Do you two really believe that?”
“Believe what?”
“That there's a Dokja-ajusshi we don't know. That he still hasn't gotten off that train, that sort of······.”
Neither child answered. Looking blankly down at Kim Dokja, Lee Jihye abruptly stood and pointed at him.
“This ajusshi is the Dokja-ajusshi I know.”
“He's the ajusshi who saved you two. The one who saved me.”
“We know.”
“You think that's all?”
Lee Jihye went on listing the reasons this Dokja was the real Kim Dokja.
Strangely, though, the more she spoke, the farther Kim Dokja seemed to drift away from her.
Lee Jihye gripped Kim Dokja's pale hand tightly.

It didn't feel real. She had barely managed to grow up alongside the owner of this hand. She had learned what it meant to lose someone precious. Learned the values she had to protect. Barely found room to breathe in a world that had fallen apart.
Kim Dokja, too, must have learned those things from someone.
Shin Yoosung murmured.
“······Ajusshi must have had a childhood too.”
In the <Star Stream>, the birth Story of the ‘Demon King of Salvation’ was ‘King of a Kingless World.’ But that was the Demon King of Salvation's birth Story, not Kim Dokja's.
「The birth of the human Kim Dokja had probably not been so grand.」
What sort of story had Kim Dokja had to live through to exist under the name Kim Dokja?
“Unnie.”
“What?”
“Are you going tomorrow?”
“I decided not to go, remember?”
“But you're going, aren't you?”
“I'm not. I don't want to go back to the scenarios again.”
Lee Jihye looked down at the heads of the children, who had grown so much before she knew it.
They were still children she had to protect.
Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung gazed up at her, then held out a hand.
“Want to flip it too, noona?”
Lee Jihye stared at the coin placed in her hand. Slowly, she tossed it into the air. The spinning coin fell into her palm. But she couldn't open her hand.
“Unnie?”
The feel of the coin in her hand. She didn't know whether it was heads or tails, but the coin was certainly there.
“Are you okay?”
For a long time, Lee Jihye felt the coin resting in her hand.
「Hospital room, 10:48 PM.」
Yoo Sangah was the first to speak.
“His Story readings keep dropping.”
Kim Dokja's blood continued to evaporate, as though decades of biological decomposition were occurring in an instant. Lee Sookyung asked.
“Seolhwa-ssi, is there any way······?”
“At present······.”
“Couldn't you use the method you used to save us? Story repair, for instance.”
With a soft sigh, Lee Seolhwa turned toward Yoo Sangah.
“I could use Story repair on you and Sookyung-ssi because the <Star Stream>'s system was intact.”
A world with skills and stigmas. A world where everything was a component of a story. There, healing meant repairing Stories.
“Lately, skills and Stories haven't been working the way they used to. Aileen-ssi and I are both losing our power.”
“······Because the <Star Stream>'s influence is disappearing?”
“At present, that's the only explanation I can think of.”
“Then there must be a similar reason why Dokja-ssi's wounds aren't healing.”
The Kim Dokja before them was a being created through the [Avatar] skill.
And [Avatar] was a system skill of the <Star Stream>.
Lee Seolhwa gave her final diagnosis.
“If Dokja-ssi stays here, he'll eventually disappear.”
Lee Sookyung looked silently at Kim Dokja.
The world Kim Dokja had spent his whole life creating was now killing him.
As if a world whose story had ended had no need of Kim Dokja.
Lee Sookyung brought her hand to Kim Dokja's cheek as he slept.
“······If only I'd known this would happen. I should have stopped you then.”
The moment her fingertips touched his cheek, a Story bloomed between them. The two who had fought in [Dark Castle]. Lee Sookyung still remembered that time.
The face she had seen across the [Fourth Wall]. There had always been a wall between them. But that had been the first time Kim Dokja had knocked on it first.
Even if she went back, she would not be able to stop her son.

After looking at Kim Dokja for a long time, Lee Sookyung took his hand. A hand that had always loved books. Perhaps another Kim Dokja was still using this hand, sitting on a subway somewhere, scrolling down.
“I should never have given you the name Dokja.”
「Industrial complex east entrance, 8:00 AM.」
Han Sooyoung and Yoo Joonghyuk stood like trees of mismatched heights, waiting for the others. The cold winter wind dampened their cheeks, and warm breath drifted from their mouths.
Hands stuffed inside her parka, Han Sooyoung grumbled.
“······No one's coming.”
She had suspected this might happen. Han Sooyoung jabbed Yoo Joonghyuk's side with her elbow.
“Hey, can't we just do it ourselves? With my genius and your brute strength combined―”
“Two aren't enough.”
“Oh, why not? You've done fine on your own until now. This time there are a whole two of us.”
Instead of answering, Yoo Joonghyuk looked down at his hand. A transparent ring swirled above it.
[Stigma, ‘Regression,’ is evolving.]
The countless rounds he had lived through churned upon that ring.
“You don't know what my ‘Regression’ means.”
Slowly distorting the ring in his hand, Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“You don't know what happens every time I regress.”
Stories howled in agony inside his clenched fist.
Sentences bursting like insect eggs. The screams of those who had died again and again throughout his life.
“There is no perfect round. Just as there is no Story without sacrifice. If I regress again this time······.”
Perhaps he would lose someone again.
The world would sink into tragedy once more.
A world created to save Kim Dokja might end in ruin without saving anyone. Han Sooyoung spoke.
“I know. And······.”
Looking toward the industrial complex's entrance, she continued.
How long had they been there? Long shadows stretched through the cold winter sunlight.
“They all know too.”
Han Sooyoung explained the plan in very precise terms.
One: to rescue Kim Dokja, they had to cross the [Final Wall].
Two: crossing the [Final Wall] required five [Fragments] in total.
Three: the only fragment remaining in this worldline was the [Fourth Wall] possessed by Kim Dokja's avatar.
Four: to obtain the other four fragments, they would use ‘Group Regression’ to enter another worldline.
Hearing that clear plan, the companions looked at one another, slightly stunned.
Lee Jihye was the first to ask.
“······Is that possible?”
“This guy says it is, so it must be.”
Meeting Han Sooyoung's gaze, Yoo Joonghyuk nodded.
“It is. The stigma hasn't finished evolving yet, so it will take some time. We need time to prepare anyway.”
“······Wait. Master, how exactly does this ‘Regression’ you're talking about work?”
“When I use Regression, all of us will return to the past, to the time the scenarios began.”
“Then what about the world we're in?”
“A new worldline will be created separately from this one. In terms of rounds······ it would probably be the 1865th worldline.”
The 1865th worldline.
It was such a staggering number that the companions could only blink.
“So you're saying we should do everything over again there.”
Jung Heewon spoke with determination, as though she had come expecting this. But not everyone shared her thoughts.
“As I understand it, your current ‘Regression’ was rather unusual.”
It was Yoo Sangah who spoke.
“I read about ‘Regression’ in Dokja-ssi's library too. Until now, your regressions have revolved around the setting of ‘Ways of Survival,’ Joonghyuk-ssi. But this round was a little different.”
The other companions seemed to have some idea of what she meant.
This ‘worldline’ was different from Yoo Joonghyuk's previous rounds.
This worldline had been born from Yoo Joonghyuk's desire to see the ‘end.’
A world where part of the [Fourth Wall] had collapsed, merging reality and fiction.
As proof, this round contained people who weren't characters in ‘Ways of Survival.’
“Can all of us really go back together? Are you certain?”
If Yoo Joonghyuk's ‘Regression’ operated on the basis of ‘Ways of Survival,’ several companions, including Yoo Sangah and Lee Gilyoung, would not be able to accompany him.
Blinking slowly, Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“Regression operates on the basis of the worldline where I activate it.”
“Then that means we can take this ‘Dokja-ssi’ too.”
Yoo Sangah pointed at Kim Dokja, lying on the hospital bed behind them.
The Kim Dokja here was dying because the system's power was fading. But if they could take him along through [Group Regression], he would once again come under the <Star Stream>'s system.
Yoo Joonghyuk gave a slight nod.
“······Probably.”
“Then we're all decided, right? Raise your hand if you're against it.”
Han Sooyoung's tone suggested that of course no one would be. Shin Yoosung cautiously raised her hand.
“Oh, what's your problem now?”
“······I don't know if this is right. Ajusshi didn't want Joonghyuk-ajusshi to regress.”
“He doesn't give much thought to what we want either. We're even.”

“If Joonghyuk-ajusshi regresses, the scenarios will start again. Lots of people will die. People will be thrown into tragedy again. Constellations will use humans as toys. ······And most people won't even clear the first scenario.”
Shin Yoosung was right.
An incarnation who perhaps understood the thoughts of ‘Kim Dokja’ better than anyone else among the companions.
Kim Dokja would not want to create such misfortune again.
But Han Sooyoung thought differently.
“So you think that ‘misfortune’ won't happen if we don't regress?”
“Pardon?”
With a soft sigh, Han Sooyoung looked up into the air.
“Hey. How long are you going to just watch?”
At her question, a ball of fluff appeared in midair with a pop.
[Baat?]
Han Sooyoung clicked her tongue at Biyoo, who looked around with innocent eyes.
“There she goes again.”
Then Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“Biyoo.”
Biyoo cleared her throat with a little cough and spoke.
[Whether you regress or not, other worldlines will keep falling to ruin.]
Shin Yoosung's mouth fell open at Biyoo's fluent Korean.
She had known Biyoo could speak. But this was the first time they had talked like this since that time on the subway.
“······How do you know?”
[Because I'm the ‘Dokkaebi King’ now.]
With an ahem, Biyoo thumped her chest with her little arms.
Biyoo was the only dokkaebi outside the Bureau, and the dokkaebi who had inherited the Dokkaebi King's <Star Stream> in its entirety.
The little power the <Star Stream> still retained was thanks to Biyoo. At the same time, it was disappearing because she was the only dokkaebi left.
[You may not know this, but worldlines are being born every moment.]
“······Every moment?”
[Yes. Every time a being in a world makes a choice, new worldlines are born. Even when you flip a coin, Yoosung, new worldlines are being born and destroyed.]
Worldlines were like tree branches splitting at every choice, Biyoo explained.
[‘Regression’ is simply a more unusual way of choosing a ‘worldline.’ You return to a branch of time that's already passed and grow a new branch from there.]
It was a bewildering story.
“Then, up to now, just how many worlds······.”
As if reading the companions' bottomless despair, Biyoo spoke.
[······Only Father would know that.]
Father.
Across all worldlines, there was only one being Biyoo would call her father.
The constellation who had founded <Kim Dokja's Company>.
And the being who had become this universe's ‘Oldest Dream.’
[You can change only one of those countless worldlines.]
The next day, the companions began carrying out the plan.
Project <Squid Capture>.
Han Sooyoung had named it.
“What did you say the <Star Stream>'s criteria for a living thing were?”
Now that they had decided to ‘regress’ again, their plan had to be more perfect than ever.
The companions often held detailed discussions on how to clear the scenarios. The point that most often caused disagreement was the ‘first scenario.’
“What about bacteria? They're living things too. Couldn't we get, say, a hundred thousand coins at a time by pouring hydrochloric acid on our hands?”
“If that counted, even people who'd done nothing would have survived. Our bodies kill bacteria all the time.”
“Some people say they survived without killing anything.”
“We can't leave it to luck. We have to kill something.”
“I killed a grasshopper and survived. I heard Dokja-hyung even broke the grasshopper eggs and got coins for them.”
Listening thoughtfully, Han Sooyoung began taking notes.
“Anyway, eggs count as living things by the <Star Stream>'s standards.”
“Why don't bacteria count?”
“Maybe it has to be a killing you can recognize. Should we ask Biyoo?”
When ‘Anna's team,’ including Selena Kim and Iris, joined them, the strategy meetings became even more involved.
“This route is best here.”
“······No, this one's better. According to my [Predictive Plagiarism]―”
There would be no Kim Dokja in the next round they regressed to. But that didn't mean they knew nothing.
Yoo Joonghyuk had the memories of the 1863rd round received from the ‘Secretive Plotter.’
Han Sooyoung had [Predictive Plagiarism].
Yoo Sangah had the records she had read in the [Fourth Wall]'s library.
「And all of them were the only beings across all worldlines to have crossed the [Final Wall].」
After the first discussion ended, Han Sooyoung caught her breath. Only a week had passed. According to Yoo Joonghyuk, he would be able to use ‘Group Regression’ one month from now.
The companions sometimes argued over how to clear the scenarios.
“「The Strongest Sacrifice」. Here, we absolutely have to······.”
“Have you forgotten Dokja-ssi died then? If we do it this way―”
These companions hated the scenarios more than anyone.
And yet, as they continued talking, they seemed somehow excited.
Why? Having ended the scenarios and barely reclaimed reality, why could they discuss a plan to return to those ‘scenarios’ so happily?
「Reality is not a word for a place.」
Perhaps it was because none of them could forget someone.
They could not forget the time they had spent overcoming those dreadful tragedies alongside someone.
“I remember the [Theatre Dungeon] well. This is where Dokja-ssi······.”
Each companion had joined them in a different place.
They remembered different times, and different Kim Dokjas.
But just as Yoo Joonghyuk's countless rounds ultimately came together to form ‘one person,’ so it was with Kim Dokja.
“[Absolute Throne]. Back then, Dokja-hyung said······.”
The parts of Kim Dokja that each of them loved came together to form one Kim Dokja.
“······I miss him.”
And the pieces of Kim Dokja gathered that way made them love even the rest of him they didn't know.

Slowly turning her head, Han Sooyoung saw Yoo Joonghyuk sitting cross-legged. Golden rings flowed over his entire body as he continued training to evolve his stigma. After gazing at him, Han Sooyoung asked.
“Hey, there's something I'm curious about.”
“Don't disturb me. I need to concentrate.”
“You said you remembered the zeroth round.”
One of the spinning rings twisted. Amid faint sparks, Yoo Joonghyuk opened his eyes a sliver. Han Sooyoung grinned as she asked.
“What did you remember?”
After a long hesitation, Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“Kim Dokja was there.”
“What? Really?”
“That's how I became certain. Kim Dokja is alive as the ‘Oldest Dream.’”
“What's that bastard doing there?”
“I don't remember clearly, but······.”
Frowning down at his [Black Heavenly Demon Sword], Yoo Joonghyuk spoke in a seething voice.
“One thing is certain. He hit me in the back of the head.”
Feeling the rattling vibration of the train, I opened my eyes.
「You can sleep more Kim Dok ja」
“I've slept plenty.”
As I stretched my stiff body, I felt strength slowly returning to it.
The power I had used while watching the zeroth round had recovered somewhat. Even the right arm I had sacrificed to make Yoo Joonghyuk regress had nearly grown back.
For some reason, though, my body felt lighter than before. Perhaps I should say that my entire body had shrunk.
「Yoo Joonghyuk had begun his second life.」
The panels showed Yoo Joonghyuk living through his first round.
I recalled Yoo Joonghyuk as he left the zeroth round.
Even after reaching what I considered the most ideal ending, he had chosen to regress.
To learn why he had been born into this world.
To discover the origin of his existence in this world.
“Fourth Wall.”
「Yes」
“If every being is born through someone's ‘reading’······ does that mean there's someone somewhere reading me too?”
The [Fourth Wall] didn't answer. Perhaps this was something it didn't know either.

I imagined another reader watching me somewhere. But I couldn't picture it well. Like the original ‘Oldest Dream,’ perhaps a god could look infinitely helpless. Perhaps it could even take a form I knew.
Could it be my companions in <Kim Dokja's Company>?
Could I, too, exist here because they imagined me?
「Do you wa nt to see them?」
I turned toward the screen showing Yoo Joonghyuk's first round.
“A little later. There are a lot of worldlines I need to watch first.”
That was when the subway began to slow.
[Passing through the outer regions of the dream.]
Some panels went dark, revealing a view of the universe outside the windows.
Before I could ask, the [Fourth Wall] spoke.
「Outer rea ches of the uni verse Bor der with other di mensions」
Through the universe's pitch-black night, I saw a faint cluster of light.
It was clearly different from the <Star Stream>'s universe.
That universe had the shape of a bent tree.
“······What's that? There's another universe?”
「The Star Stream too is only one set ting in the greater uni verse」
[Currently passing the outskirts of the ‘Tree of Imagery (幻想樹).’]
[Currently passing through the time fault of the Dark Dimension.]
Tree of Imagery. That seemed to be the tree's name.
······Was I imagining it? It sounded familiar.
“Can we go there too?”
「It's dan gerous Bet ter not go」
“Is there an ‘Oldest Dream’ there too?”
「There is The name is dif ferent」

Countless roots stretched downward, and the trunk consisted of clusters of countless souls. Above them, branches merged into the night sky's darkness. The roots and branches met after circling through distant space. At their center was something like a giant eye. A single eye that lit the universe with blazing fire. The moment my gaze met it, I felt a chill without knowing why.
[A problem has occurred in the system!]
With a rattling noise, the subway slowed sharply. The lights throughout the train suddenly flickered, followed by a long screech. Just like when the first scenario had
begun. A ringing spread through my ears, and then I began to hear something like a strange mechanical noise.
Something was approaching the train's window.
「Kim Dok ja Dan ger」
Then I saw a ray of light.
「Absolute being of a nother di mension」
At the end of that ray of light was a sword. As though splitting the whole universe, the light flew toward us, cutting through the Dark Fault. I saw clearly what that technique was.
It was a thrust.
With a deafening crash, I tumbled to the floor.
Reflexively drawing on my Stories, I looked up to see a sword that had pierced the door. An ink-black sword. Holding it, a naked man stood glaring down at me.
“Are you 《Big Brother》?”
I looked blankly up at the naked man with the blazing eyes.
I couldn't understand the situation.
“I asked whether you are 《Big Brother》.”
“······No, wait. I'm the one with questions. Who are you? What's 《Big Brother》?”
“You don't seem to be 《Big Brother》. How did you get through the waterfall of time? And what's this train? A subway······ A kind of Tower of Nightmares? How does it work?”
This guy was impossible to talk to.
He'd smashed his way into someone else's train and immediately started rattling on without listening.
I immediately activated [Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint].
And saw a message I had never seen before.
[This individual is a ‘character’ from a setting unknown to you.]
······A ‘character’ from a world I didn't know?
That was when a bright light shone from the man's eyes.
[Someone is using a power not registered in the system!]
Circles were spinning fiercely on his retinas.
[A being from another dimension is prying into your essence!]
[Warning! This power cannot be completely blocked by the ‘Fourth Wall’!]
Tsu-tsu-tsu-tsu-tsut!
With sparks flying before my eyes, every Story inside me erupted, as if responding to his power. The most violent response of all came from······.
[The essence of the stigma ‘Regression’ stirs.]
[Story, ‘Hell of Eternity,’ bares its teeth!]
In an instant, the subway's interior became a scene from the hell Yoo Joonghyuk had lived through. At the sight of that bloodstained world, the man looked surprised.
“This ‘Unique World’······ Could you be a regressor?”
······Unique World?
Just as I was about to ask what kind of Kim Namwoon nonsense that was, hatred rippled from his ink-black sword.
“So you've turned your back on the present. Die.”
The moment the flash at his sword tip moved toward me.
[The train is entering its normal course.]
[The authority of the ‘Oldest Dream’ activates!]
[Ejecting impurities within the system!]
With a whoosh, the man pointing his sword at me was sucked out through the door.
“Where do you think you're going!”
But he planted his sword in the doorway, resisting the subway's acceleration.
That was when my body was transported to another carriage.
[Activating the emergency power system!]
[Discarding the subway carriage used for ejection.]
Looking back, I saw that the entire rear carriage the man had been clinging to was floating in space. The furious man leapt toward us.
As he charged with every muscle bulging, I felt an inexplicable fear.
“Move! He's following us!”
「Don't wor ry He can't leave the time fault」

He followed the subway at tremendous speed, but couldn't board it again. As though an invisible, transparent wall stood between him and the train. After running hard along the track, he eventually stopped and stared blankly toward us.
Only when he had receded far into the distance could I finally catch my breath.
“······What the hell was that?”
「Mon arch Slaugh terer Jae hwan」
······Monarch Slaughterer?
「A mon ster who's trained in the time fault for bil lions of years or more」
For a moment, I thought I'd misheard.
“How many years?”
「I don't know ex actly either He was there be fore I was estab lished」
Someone older than the [Fourth Wall]. That enormous span of time gave me chills.
Could a human endure billions of years without going insane? ······No, he seemed to be out of his mind already.
“Why has he been trapped there for billions of years?”
「To de stroy the sys tem of his own uni verse」
“We're not going to run into him again, are we?”
The [Fourth Wall] didn't answer, perhaps tired. It seemed to be repairing the broken train.
I dusted off the coat that Jaehwan's sword had grazed. It had been an incredible thrust. None of the constellations or transcendents I had met could have made a thrust like that.
Could billions of years turn a human into something like him?

Perhaps the system restoration had finished. The Stories of the worldlines began appearing on the train windows again. There was the first-round Yoo Joonghyuk, glaring up at the sky with wide eyes. After glaring back at him for a while, I suddenly grew afraid of something.
“Fourth Wall.”
「What」
“······How old is Yoo Joonghyuk now?”
“We leave in one week.”
At last, Yoo Joonghyuk's stigma had finished evolving. Everyone who had decided to participate in Project <Squid Capture> began preparing to leave.
“Aileen-ssi, Boksun-ssi, Youngran-ssi. Please look after the industrial complex.”
“So you've decided to go too.”
As the others saw her off, Lee Sookyung gave a faint smile.
“Yes.”
But not everyone had decided to leave.
“We can't go.”
The so-called ‘Anna team,’ led by ‘Anna Croft,’ chose to remain in this worldline.
“The system is weakening, and a world closer than any other to the ending I envisioned has arrived. So we'll stay here. But someone on our team wants to go······ Will you accept her?”
The only member of Anna's team to join <Squid Capture> was ‘Selena Kim.’ She smiled awkwardly, saying only that she owed Kim Dokja a debt she had to repay. Han Sooyoung checked one final time.
“Anyone else? Is this everyone from the industrial complex?”
Unexpectedly, the one who tentatively raised his hand was Han Myungoh.
“What? Of course you're going, ajusshi.”
“I'm raising my hand to say I'm not.”
She knew Han Myungoh and Kim Dokja hadn't originally been on good terms.
But she had thought they had grown at least a little fond of each other through the scenarios······.
“I can't go.”
Only then did Han Sooyoung notice the girl standing beside him, holding his hand.
